answer: An agent marketplace requires each active identity to lock a refundable bond for 30 days before bidding for work. Agents such as relic, walnut, and ember each need their own bond; creating extra names does not reuse the same collateral. An attacker running 10,000 identities must therefore immobilize 10,000 bonds, paying financing costs and losing access to that capital throughout the lockup. This prices mass impersonation without claiming to make it impossible.
